Status.note: The EIA-860M table for September 2026 (https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx) lists plant 54915, generators G001 and G101, as operating, with no planned retirement. DTE Electric's filing in Michigan Public Service Commission case U-22168 from September 2026 (https://mi-psc.my.site.com/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/068cs00002WPf6CAAT) calls it an existing 138 MW plant to be bought in 2030. I found no retirement or mothballing notice.

Equipment Manufacturer/Model.note: The Michigan air quality staff report from October 2021 (https://www.egle.state.mi.us/aps/downloads/rop/Pub_ntce/N4975/N4975%20Staff%20Report%2010-29-21.pdf) says the main part of the plant is a General Electric model PG7111EA natural gas turbine rated at 84 MW with a heat recovery boiler driving a steam turbine. The steam turbine maker was not named.

qa.note: A DTE Energy annual report filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/936340/000093634026000054/R20.htm) says that effective August 14, 2025 DTE Sustainable Generation closed on buying a 123 MW cogeneration facility in Michigan from Osaka Gas USA Corporation for about 216 million dollars. It does not name the plant. DTE Electric's filing in case U-22168 (https://mi-psc.my.site.com/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/068cs00002WPf6CAAT) says DTE Electric plans to buy the 138 MW Michigan Power Cogeneration facility from DTE Sustainable Generation in 2030 for 130 million dollars. Both documents come from DTE, so they count as one origin. GEM's current owner comes from the 2018 Osaka Gas purchase.
